title: Normality and integrality of a smooth-generic nodal trait family
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$, uniformizer $\pi$, residue field $k$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to T$ be flat and finitely presented [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose $X_F$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose each nonempty geometric fibre is reduced of pure dimension one, and every nonsmooth closed point of such a fibre over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then every local ring of $X$ is an integrally closed domain. The open subscheme $X_F$ is dense in $X$. If $X_F$ is integral, then $X$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Neither projectivity nor connectedness of the geometric fibres is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family), specialized to a DVR with smooth generic fibre; normality follows from the xy=pi^n local calculation. Agent-formulated global consequence, carrying returned Step 1; supporting de Jong, Lemma 3.13 proof, printed p.609 (primary PDF read online; archival PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-finite-singular-charts] with $R=A$: its flatness, finite presentation, smooth generic fibre and geometric nodal-fibre hypotheses are exactly ours, including empty or disconnected fibres. Thus $X$ is Noetherian and the nonsmooth locus $Z$ is a finite set of closed special-fibre points. Every point outside $Z$ has a regular total-space local ring, and every $z\in Z$ has $\dim\mathcal O_{X,z}=2$. Consequently every point with local dimension at most one lies outside $Z$ and is regular. We use the nonsmooth locus here, not the potentially smaller nonregular locus: a node with chart exponent $n=1$ can already be regular. These conclusions are clauses of the cited statement; no completion or excellence assertion is needed.

The ordinary special fibre $X_k$ is reduced: apply [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-algebraic-closure-test] to $X_k/k$, whose base change to an algebraic closure is reduced by hypothesis, and then take the identity field extension $k/k$. This includes the empty special fibre. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme], every local ring of $X_k$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 035X (lemma-geometrically-reduced), algebraic-closure test; reducedness for the identity extension

proof.text: Put $W=X\setminus Z$. It is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are regular by step 1; [def-weil-regular-scheme] therefore makes $W$ regular. At $x\in W$, choose a regular Noetherian affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset W$, as that definition permits. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal], $C$ is normal, so [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal] gives $(S_2)$ for $C$. The identification $C_{\mathfrak p_x}\simeq\mathcal O_{X,x}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] transfers its depth bound: $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{X,x}\ge\min(2,\dim\mathcal O_{X,x})$. Here the stalk is unchanged on the open neighbourhood $V$, directly from restriction of the structure sheaf.

Fix $z\in Z$ and set $S=\mathcal O_{X,z}$ and $Q=S/\pi S$. Flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism] gives a flat local map $A\to S$; both rings are Noetherian. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], $Q$ is the actual local ring of $X_k$ at $z$, so is reduced by step 2. Apply the local form of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to $A\to S$ at their maximal ideals. Since $\dim A=1$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and $\dim S=2$ by step 1, it gives $\dim Q=1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-reduced], the reduced Noetherian local ring $Q$ satisfies $(S_1)$ and hence has depth at least one. The uniformizer $\pi$ is a nonzerodivisor in the domain $A$ and $A/\pi A=k\ne0$, so it is a regular sequence of length one and $\operatorname{depth}A\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Now [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] yields $\operatorname{depth}S=\operatorname{depth}A+\operatorname{depth}Q\ge2$. This treats every point not covered by step 3.

Choose any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ in a Noetherian affine cover of $X$. Under [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], all $B_{\mathfrak p}$ are the corresponding local rings of $X$. Step 1 makes them regular whenever $\dim B_{\mathfrak p}\le1$, and steps 3--4 give their depth bounds $\operatorname{depth}B_{\mathfrak p}\ge\min(2,\dim B_{\mathfrak p})$. These are exactly $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal] to the Noetherian ring $B$: every $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is an integrally closed domain. The affine cover and its stalk identifications prove the first conclusion for every point of $X$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], $f$ is open. If $O\subset X$ is any nonempty open, then $f(O)$ is a nonempty open of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Such an open contains its generic point: the only points of the spectrum of a DVR are $(0)$ and $(\pi)$, and every open containing $(\pi)$ contains $(0)$. Thus $O$ meets the generic fibre. Since $\operatorname{Spec}F=D(\pi)\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$, its inverse image is exactly the open subscheme $X_F$, and we have proved that $X_F$ is dense. If $X$ is empty the density assertion is immediate.

source.place: Tag 01UA (lemma-fppf-open); elementary topology of the spectrum of a DVR

proof.text: Finally assume $X_F$ is integral. It is nonempty and irreducible by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. For closed subsets $C,D\subset X$ with $X=C\cup D$, the intersections with $X_F$ give a closed cover of $X_F$, so irreducibility gives $X_F\subset C$ or $X_F\subset D$. Density from step 6 then gives $X=C$ or $X=D$, proving that $X$ is irreducible and nonempty. Every local ring of $X$ is a domain by step 5, hence reduced: a nilpotent element in a domain is zero. Thus $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and the equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme] proves that $X$ is integral. No connectedness or projectivity has entered the argument.

lean.statement: theorem normal_dense_integral_of_smooth_generic_nodal_trait (A : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra A F] [IsFractionRing A F] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec A) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (hgeneric : Smooth (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A F))))) (hfibres : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (g : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec A), IsReduced (pullback (C := Scheme) f g) ∧ (pullback (C := Scheme) f g).IsPureDimension 1 ∧ ∀ z : pullback (C := Scheme) f g, IsClosed ({z} : Set (pullback (C := Scheme) f g)) → ¬ ((NodalFiber.projection f Ω g).stalkMap z).hom.FormallySmooth → Nonempty (NodalFiber.completedLocalRing z ≃+* NodalFiber.powerSeriesQuotient Ω)) : (∀ x : X, IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ DenseRange (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A F)))) ∧ (IsIntegral (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A F)))) → IsIntegral X)
